arxiv-2009-06027.title: ReviewViz: Assisting Developers Perform Empirical Study on Energy Consumption Related Reviews for Mobile Applications Conference: IEEE/ACM 7th International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and Systems; October 5–6, 2020; Seoul, Republic of Korea IEEE/ACM 7th International Conference on Mob
arxiv-2009-06027.creator: Mohammad Abdul Hadi, Fatemeh Hendijani Fard
arxiv-2009-06027.description: Abstract . Improving energy efficiency of mobile applications is a topic that has gained a lot of attention recently. It has been addressed in a number of ways such as identifying energy bugs and developing a catalog of energy patterns.

arxiv-2204-07324.title: Joint DoA-Range Estimation Using Space-Frequency Virtual Difference Coarray Thanks: Z. Mao, S. Liu, L. Han, and Y. Huang were supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant Nos. 62001103 and U1936201 and the Basic Research Program of Jiangsu Province under Grant No
arxiv-2204-07324.creator: Zihuan Mao, Shengheng Liu
arxiv-2204-07324.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the problem of joint direction-of-arrival (DoA) and range estimation using frequency diverse coprime array (FDCA). By incorporating the coprime array structure and coprime frequency offsets, a two-dimensional space-frequency virtual difference coarray corresponding to uniform array and uniform frequency offset is considered to increase the number of degrees-of-freedom (DoFs).

arxiv-2207-02539.title: Learning Regularized Multi-Scale Feature Flow for High Dynamic Range Imaging
arxiv-2207-02539.creator: Qian Ye, Masanori Suganuma, Jun Xiao, Takayuki Okatani
arxiv-2207-02539.description: Abstract Reconstructing ghosting-free high dynamic range (HDR) images of dynamic scenes from a set of multi-exposure images is a challenging task, especially with large object motion and occlusions, leading to visible artifacts using existing methods. To address this problem, we propose a deep network that tries to learn multi-scale feature flow guided by the regularized loss.

arxiv-2208-00549.title: Unifying Approaches in Active Learning and Active Sampling via Fisher Information and Information-Theoretic Quantities
arxiv-2208-00549.creator: Andreas Kirsch andreas.kirsch@cs.ox.ac.uk
arxiv-2208-00549.description: Abstract Recently proposed methods in data subset selection, that is active learning and active sampling, use Fisher information, Hessians, similarity matrices based on gradients, and gradient lengths to estimate how informative data is for a model’s training. Are these different approaches connected, and if so, how?

arxiv-2208-08655.title: Generating Synthetic Clinical Data that Capture Class Imbalanced Distributions with Generative Adversarial Networks: Example using Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV
arxiv-2208-08655.creator: Nicholas I-Hsien Kuo, Federico Garcia, Anders Sönnerborg, Maurizio Zazzi, Michael Böhm, Rolf Kaiser, Mark Polizzotto, Louisa Jorm, Sebastiano Barbieri
arxiv-2208-08655.description: Abstract Clinical data usually cannot be freely distributed due to their highly confidential nature and this hampers the development of machine learning in the healthcare domain. One way to mitigate this problem is by generating realistic synthetic datasets using generative adversarial networks (GANs). However, GANs are known to suffer from mode collapse thus creating outputs of low diversity.

arxiv-2209-03567.title: SOM-Net: Unrolling the Subspace-based Optimization for Solving Full-wave Inverse Scattering Problems
arxiv-2209-03567.creator: Yu Liu, Hao Zhao, Rencheng Song, Xudong Chen, Chang Li, Xun Chen
arxiv-2209-03567.description: Abstract In this paper, an unrolling algorithm of the iterative subspace-based optimization method (SOM) is proposed for solving full-wave inverse scattering problems (ISPs). The unrolling network, named SOM-Net, inherently embeds the Lippmann-Schwinger physical model into the design of network structures. The SOM-Net takes the deterministic induced current and the raw permittivity image obtained from back-propagation (BP) as the input.

arxiv-2310-04114.title: Aorta Segmentation from 3D CT in MICCAI SEG.A. 2023 Challenge.
arxiv-2310-04114.creator: Andriy Myronenko, Dong Yang, Yufan He, Daguang Xu
arxiv-2310-04114.description: Abstract Aorta provides the main blood supply of the body. Screening of aorta with imaging helps for early aortic disease detection and monitoring. In this work, we describe our solution to the Segmentation of the Aorta (SEG.A.23 1 1 1 https://multicenteraorta.grand-challenge.org/multicenteraorta/ ) from 3D CT challenge. We use automated segmentation method Auto3DSeg 2 2 2 https://monai.

arxiv-2401-00960.title: A refined search for high-velocity gas in the Cygnus Loop supernova remnant
arxiv-2401-00960.creator: Adam M. Ritchey, S. R. Federman, David L. Lambert
arxiv-2401-00960.description: Abstract We present the results of a sensitive search for high-velocity gas in interstellar absorption lines associated with the Cygnus Loop supernova remnant (SNR). We examine high-resolution, high signal-to-noise ratio optical spectra of six stars in the Cygnus Loop region with distances greater than ∼ \sim 700 pc. All stars show low-velocity Na i and Ca ii absorption.

arxiv-2504-05422.title: EP-Diffuser: An Efficient Diffusion Model for Traffic Scene Generation and Prediction via Polynomial Representations
arxiv-2504-05422.creator: Yue Yao, Mohamed-Khalil Bouzidi, Daniel Goehring, Joerg Reichardt
arxiv-2504-05422.description: Abstract As the prediction horizon increases, predicting the future evolution of traffic scenes becomes increasingly difficult due to the multi-modal nature of agent motion. Most state-of-the-art (SotA) prediction models primarily focus on forecasting the most likely future. However, for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles, it is equally important to cover the distribution for plausible motion alternatives.

arxiv-2510-07470.title: Provably Accelerated Imaging with Restarted Inertia and Score-based Image Priors
arxiv-2510-07470.creator: Marien Renaud 1, †, Julien Hermant 1, †, Deliang Wei 2, †, and Yu Sun 2, ✉
arxiv-2510-07470.description: Abstract Fast convergence and high-quality image recovery are two essential features of algorithms for solving ill-posed imaging inverse problems. Existing methods, such as regularization by denoising (RED) , often focus on designing sophisticated image priors to improve reconstruction quality, while leaving convergence acceleration to heuristics.

arxiv-2510-26592.title: Ring-polymer instanton theory for tunneling between asymmetric wells
arxiv-2510-26592.creator: Marit R. Fiechter, Gabriel Laude, Jeremy O. Richardson
arxiv-2510-26592.description: Abstract Instanton theory has arisen as a practical tool for calculating tunneling splittings in molecular systems. Unfortunately, the original formulation of instanton theory fundamentally breaks down when trying to calculate the level splitting in asymmetric double wells, as there is no imaginary-time periodic orbit connecting the two non-degenerate minima.

arxiv-2511-05961.title: Photodiode quantum efficiency for 2-µm light in the signal band of gravitational wave detectors Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2511-05961.creator: Julian Gurs 1,†, Nils Sültmann 1,†, Christian Darsow-Fromm 2, Sebastian Steinlechner 3,4 and Roman Schnabel 1,*
arxiv-2511-05961.description: Abstract Quantum technologies with quantum correlated light require photodiodes with near-perfect ‘true’ quantum efficiency, the definition of which adequately accounts for the photodiode dark noise. Future squeezed-light-enhanced gravitational wave detectors could in principle achieve higher sensitivities with a longer laser wavelength around 2 µm.

arxiv-2512-25043.title: Thin Tree Verification is coNP-Complete
arxiv-2512-25043.creator: Alice Moayyedi
arxiv-2512-25043.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alice Moayyedi. An α \alpha -thin tree T T of a graph G G is a spanning tree such that every cut of G G has at most an α \alpha proportion of its edges in T T . The thin tree conjecture proposes that there exists a function f f such that for any α > 0 \alpha>0 , every f ⁡ ( α ) f(\alpha) -edge-connected graph has an α \alpha -thin tree.

arxiv-2601-20061.title: Primitive-Driven Acceleration of Hyperdimensional Computing for Real-Time Image Classification
arxiv-2601-20061.creator: Dhruv Parikh, Jebacyril Arockiaraj, and Viktor Prasanna
arxiv-2601-20061.description: Abstract Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) represents data using extremely high-dimensional, low-precision vectors—termed hypervectors (HVs)—and performs learning and inference through lightweight, noise-tolerant operations. However, the high dimensionality, sparsity, and repeated data movement involved in HDC make these computations difficult to accelerate efficiently on conventional processors.

pmc-11497357.title: Current Challenges to Align Inflammatory Key Events in Animals and Lung Cell Models In Vitro
pmc-11497357.creator: Isidora Loncarevic, Seyran Mutlu, Martina Dzepic, Sandeep Keshavan, Alke Petri-Fink, Fabian Blank, Barbara Rothen-Rutishauser
pmc-11497357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). With numerous novel and innovative in vitro models emerging every year to reduce or replace animal testing, there is an urgent need to align the design, harmonization, and validation of such systems using in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) approaches. In particular, in inhalation toxicology, there is a lack of predictive and prevalidated in vitro lung models that can be considered a valid alternative for animal testing.

pmc-11618044.title: Structural and Electronic Factors Controlling the Efficiency and Rate of Intersystem Crossing to the Triplet State in Thiophene Polycyclic Derivatives
pmc-11618044.creator: Cameron Griffrith, Sarah E. Krul, Sean J. Hoehn, Tram Phan, Carlos E. Crespo‐Hernández
pmc-11618044.description: Thiophene polycyclic derivatives are widely used in organic light‐emitting diodes, photovoltaics, and medicinal chemistry applications. Understanding the electronic and structural factors controlling their intersystem crossing rates is paramount for these applications to be successful. This study investigates the photophysical, electronic structure, and excited state dynamics of 1,2‐benzodiphenylene sulfide, benzo[b]naphtho[1,2‐d]thiophene, and benzo[b]naphtho[2,3‐d]thiophene in polar aprotic and non‐polar solvents.

pmc-12483449.title: The protective effects of the combination of Simmondsia chinensis extract and vitamin E on nephrotoxicity and hepatotoxicity in rats exposed to cisplatin: An anti-inflammatory and antioxidant study
pmc-12483449.creator: Ali Mohammed Khafaji, Sura Safi Khafaji
pmc-12483449.description: Background:Cisplatin (CSP), a chemotherapy drug widely used for treating solid tumors, can cause cellular toxicity in various percentages. Natural antioxidants, such as phenols, help reduce free radicals and inflammation.Aim:This study aimed to investigate the synergistic protective effects of Simmondsia chinensis extract, vitamin E, or their combination, particularly in cases of CSP-induced renal and hepatotoxicity.

pmc-12593186.title: Massive bowel intussusception requiring right hemicolectomy
pmc-12593186.creator: Jeffrey Baum, Paige Varney, Neema Patel, Maria Chimarios, Charles Thompson
pmc-12593186.description: on presentation revealed evidence of a large ileocaecal intussusception due to a 3-cm ileocaecal lipoma (figure 1), requiring an urgent robotic ileocaecal resection. In the operating room, it was noted that the intussusception could not be manually reduced, and the decision was made to transect the leading and trailing ends in situ.

pmc-12647454.title: Novel insights into the molecular mechanisms of LGMDD2: role of TNPO3 in experimental cell and zebrafish models
pmc-12647454.creator: MT Rodia, M. Fazzina, Roberta Costa, MT Altieri, G. Sabbioni, E. D’Aversa, G. Breveglieri, E. Gatto, C. Bertolucci, S. Lombardi, M. Bergonzoni, R. Casadei, S. Santi, V. Papa, S. Ratti, G. Cenacchi, M. Borgatti, F. Frabetti
pmc-12647454.description: Transportin 3 (TNPO3) is a nuclear carrier for serine/arginine-rich proteins which are essential for mRNA splicing and metabolism. Mutations in the TNPO3 gene result in a protein with an extended C-terminal domain, leading to the onset of LGMDD2, a rare form of limb girdle muscular dystrophy.

pmc-13122240.title: Pharmacology and toxicology of veterinary isoxazolines: a review
pmc-13122240.creator: Paulina Markowska-Buńka, Bartosz Rasiński, Hubert Ziółkowski
pmc-13122240.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Isoxazoline derivatives have rapidly become cornerstone ectoparasiticides in veterinary medicine, providing high efficacy and long-lasting protection against fleas, ticks, and other arthropods in companion animals and, more recently, in food-producing species. This review summarizes current knowledge on the chemistry, pharmacology, and toxicology of the main veterinary isoxazolines - fluralaner, afoxolaner, sarolaner, and lotilaner - with particular emphasis on safety profiles and broader One Health considerations.

pmc-13556481.title: 519. Baseline EEG connectivity predicts differential clinical response to donepezil and memantine in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13556481.creator: T Youn, J Eo, H-J Park, S Kim, A Moon
pmc-13556481.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and widespread disruption of large-scale brain networks. Pharmacological treatments for moderate to severe AD primarily include high-dose acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors and non-competitive antagonists of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor.
